idiom_name: test class implements the callback interface; object expression or SAM-converted lambda for one-method seams
implementation_notes: Kotlin test classes are plain classes (JUnit 5 requires no inheritance), so implementing the collaborator interface on the test class and passing this works as in Java; the more local idioms are an object expression declared beside the test, which captures fixture state and confines the double, and a SAM conversion for a fun interface, where a lambda becomes the collaborator. A SAM-converted lambda or a method-local object expression is Meszaros' Inner Test Double rather than a Self Shunt, so reach for it when only one test method needs the callback; the conformance form stays justified when several tests in the class observe the same collaborator. MockK (mockk/verify) replaces the hand-written shunt when expectations or call counts must be verified.
pitfalls: An object expression stored in a companion object or a reused suite instance is created once for many tests; declare it per-instance so JUnit's fresh-instance-per-test guarantee does the isolation for you.
A SAM lambda cannot be named or reused, so the moment a second test needs the same behaviour the double has to leave the lambda and become a class.
Callbacks from coroutines or executors mutate the recording list concurrently; confine them to the test thread or use a thread-safe collection.
